tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores registered accounts used for authentication (email/password with bcrypt hash) and role-based access (User or Administrator).

columns.name: id
columns.notes: Primary key; referenced by tasks.user_id (one user owns many tasks, ON DELETE CASCADE)

columns.name: email
columns.notes: Login identifier; store lowercased so uniqueness is case-insensitive

columns.name: password_hash
columns.notes: bcrypt hash only; never store plaintext passwords

tables.name: tasks
tables.purpose: Stores each user's tasks, including title, optional description, and completion status. Supports create, complete/reopen, delete, and filtered viewing.

columns.name: user_id
columns.notes: FK to users.id; owner of the task; ON DELETE CASCADE. Used to enforce that users only access their own tasks

columns.name: title
columns.notes: Required; empty or whitespace-only titles rejected by validation (CHECK length(trim(title)) > 0)

columns.name: is_completed
columns.notes: false = active/incomplete, true = completed; toggled to complete or reopen

columns.name: completed_at
columns.notes: Set when marked complete; set to NULL when reopened

relationships.notes: Each task belongs to exactly one user; ON DELETE CASCADE

assumptions: Database is PostgreSQL, so uuid primary keys use gen_random_uuid() (pgcrypto or PostgreSQL 13+).
Each user has exactly one role (User or Administrator), so role is a column on users rather than a roles table with a junction table; no many-to-many relationships exist in the requirements.
Authentication uses JWT, which is stateless, so no sessions or token table is stored.
Tasks are permanently deleted (hard delete) per the requirement that tasks are removed from the database; no soft-delete column is included.
Task status is a boolean (is_completed) since only active and completed states are required; completed_at records when completion occurred.
Each task belongs to exactly one user; sharing and collaboration are out of scope.
The one-to-many relationship between users and tasks is defined only on the tasks table via tasks.user_id referencing users.id (ON DELETE CASCADE); the users table holds no foreign key column.
Cross-user access (HTTP 403) is enforced in the application layer by checking tasks.user_id against the authenticated user.
The composite index (user_id, is_completed, created_at) supports listing a user's tasks, filtering by status, and sorting newest first.
Email addresses are normalized to lowercase by the application before storage to ensure unique login identifiers.
